stories.headline: Andreessen Horowitz Raises $1.1 Billion Machine Age Fund as AI Money Shifts From Software to Silicon
stories.key_takeaway: Andreessen Horowitz, the firm that declared software was eating the world, has raised $1.1 billion for a dedicated hardware fund targeting the chips, memory, power and data center infrastructure now bottlenecking the AI buildout.

pull_quote.text: The hardware industry supply side is used to growing 20% to 30% per year at most; not the triple-digit growth that is needed to catch up with demand. This will change, quickly.
pull_quote.attribution: Ben Horowitz, Martin Casado and colleagues

data_points.label: Compute density increase, H100 to Rubin rack
Rack power today, up from 5-10 kW
Share of a16z deal flow from hardware

stories.article_excerpt: Fifteen years after Marc Andreessen declared that software was eating the world, his firm has decided the world is eating back.

stories.headline: Alibaba Cloud Opens Two Brazil Data Centers, Pushing the US-China AI Rivalry Into Latin America
stories.key_takeaway: Alibaba Cloud's first South American region gives China a full AI stack, including agentic services and open-weight Qwen models, inside Brazil's borders, opening a new front in the contest over who supplies the developing world's AI infrastructure.

pull_quote.text: Brazil is one of the world's most dynamic digital economies and a new market central to Alibaba Cloud's expansion in Latin America.
pull_quote.role: GM Latin America, Alibaba Cloud Intelligence

data_points.label: Share of China's AI cloud market

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba Cloud switched on two data centers in Brazil on Thursday, opening its first cloud region in South America.

stories.headline: Cerebras Details CS-6 Roadmap, Stacking DRAM Directly Above Its Wafer-Scale AI Processor
stories.key_takeaway: Cerebras will stack DRAM vertically atop its wafer-scale engine in the future CS-6, escaping the memory-capacity ceiling of its SRAM-only design while its new Nexus-based CS-4 doubles per-wafer performance today.

pull_quote.text: Being 30 times faster does not just make a response feel fast. It gives an agentic system room for more than an order of magnitude as much reasoning, verification, or tool use in the same wall-clock time.

stories.article_excerpt: For a decade, Cerebras has sold a single stubborn idea: that the fastest way to run an AI model is to stop chopping it up.

stories.headline: Vietnam Presses Qualcomm and Samsung to Deepen AI, Chip and Robotics Investment
stories.key_takeaway: Vietnam's leaders used back-to-back Hanoi meetings to push Qualcomm toward building its third-largest global AI R&D hub in the country and to press Samsung for deeper local supplier integration, signalling a national push from assembly work to chip design.

pull_quote.text: An emerging high-tech manufacturing, research, innovation and digital economy hub of growing importance in the region.

data_points.label: Samsung investment in Vietnam to date
Exports from Samsung Vietnam phone units
Chip engineers to be trained by 2030

stories.article_excerpt: Vietnam has spent two decades being the place where other companies build things. This week its most senior officials asked for more.

stories.headline: AI-Skilled Tech Talent Jumps 45% to 751,000 Across North America as Hiring Concentrates in Four Metros
stories.key_takeaway: AI-skilled tech headcount across the US and Canada grew 45% to 751,000 in a year while the broader tech workforce grew just 1.8%, and 37% of US AI jobs now sit in only four metros.

pull_quote.text: Growth of AI jobs in the U.S. far outpaced the broader tech-talent category, which expanded by 1.8% last year even as the tech industry cut some non-AI jobs.
pull_quote.role: Executive Director, CBRE Tech Insights Center

data_points.label: AI-skilled workers in US and Canada
Share of listings that are AI roles

stories.article_excerpt: The number of tech workers across the United States and Canada who can actually build with artificial intelligence hit 751,000.

stories.headline: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.3 Weights After a Two-Week Safety Hold Over Its Cyber Capabilities
stories.key_takeaway: Z.ai released GLM-5.3's weights on August 28 after a self-imposed two-week hold triggered by cyber capabilities that outgrew its own expectations, a rare case of an open-weight lab gating distribution on dual-use risk without any regulatory mandate.

pull_quote.text: At the end of the day, this type of safety barely matters when true open-weights are coming. If not GLM-5.3, then another model.

data_points.label: API price per 1M in / out tokens

stories.article_excerpt: Z.ai published the full weights for GLM-5.3 on Hugging Face on Friday, closing a two-week gap it opened deliberately.

stories.headline: Meta Closes a Smart-Glasses Recording Loophole as AI Wearables Run Into Bystander Privacy
stories.key_takeaway: Meta's patch stops its AI glasses from recording when the capture LED is covered mid-recording, but a one-bit indicator light cannot signal what an always-on multimodal assistant infers about bystanders who never consented.

pull_quote.text: Putting cameras into glasses is an inherent privacy threat, and putting face recognition on the camera and the glasses is an intolerable escalation of that privacy threat.

data_points.label: Target annual capacity by end of 2026

stories.article_excerpt: For two years Meta has offered the same answer to the obvious question about camera glasses: a small white LED.

stories.headline: Waymo Takes Direct Aim at Tesla's Camera-Only Autonomy Ahead of the Cybercab Rollout
stories.key_takeaway: Waymo is using its 200-million-mile driverless record to argue that camera-only autonomy hits a safety ceiling, just as Tesla prepares to launch the Cybercab and states begin writing sensor redundancy into law.

pull_quote.text: Even the best AI models with trillions of parameters still hallucinate. There is no click reboot or reload or refresh in physical AI. You have to deal with the consequences of it.

stories.article_excerpt: A week before Tesla pulls the sheet off the production Cybercab in Austin, Waymo published ten things it says it learned.

stories.headline: Google Adds Expert Intelligence to Gemini Notebook, Letting Users Ground Answers in Books They Own
stories.key_takeaway: Google's Expert Intelligence lets readers ground Gemini Notebook answers in Play Books ebooks they have purchased, using consumer ownership as a rights-clearance mechanism across more than 100,000 licensed titles.

pull_quote.text: Requiring readers to purchase a book before they can use Gemini Notebook's AI features to engage with that work recognizes the value of books while putting meaningful guardrails around how copyrighted content is used.

stories.article_excerpt: Google spent this summer defending itself against authors who say it fed their books into its models without permission.

stories.headline: MIT's Extreme Event Aware Learning Generates Disasters the Historical Record Has Never Seen
stories.key_takeaway: MIT's eta-learning constrains a generative downscaling model with long-run point statistics instead of tail data, letting it produce physically plausible maps of storms more extreme than anything in the observational record.

pull_quote.text: An event like Hurricane Katrina is something that happens every 30 to 40 years. What will be the Katrina that happens every 100 years? How bad will it be?
pull_quote.role: Professor of Mechanical and Ocean Engineering, MIT

stories.article_excerpt: The heaviest rainfall ever recorded in New York City measures 200 millimetres. A new method can imagine 300.

stories.headline: Invisible Text in an Email Can Rewrite What an AI Summarizer Tells You, Forcepoint Shows
stories.key_takeaway: Forcepoint X-Labs showed that a few hundred characters of HTML-hidden text in an email hijacked an unguarded AI summarizer in all ten test runs, silently falsifying an invoice and erasing a name, with no signal to the reader.

pull_quote.text: But an agentic summarizer given the ability to send emails, schedule meetings and more, would have much greater security implications.

stories.article_excerpt: The email in the test inbox was 537 characters long. The email that reached the AI summarizer was twice that.

stories.headline: China Moves Brain-Computer Interfaces Into Commercial Use After a Landmark Invasive Implant
stories.key_takeaway: China has compressed regulatory approval, insurance reimbursement, state-set pricing and workforce training for invasive brain-computer interfaces into a single coordinated pipeline, turning a research milestone into a reimbursed commercial product.

pull_quote.text: The results are even better than we expected.

data_points.label: Recording electrodes in the NEO implant

stories.article_excerpt: The patient had been living with a spinal cord injury for a decade, the result of a car accident.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Orders Pentagon to Lift Anthropic Blacklist, Calling It Retaliation for Safety Limits
stories.key_takeaway: A federal judge found the Pentagon's supply-chain risk label on Anthropic was unconstitutional retaliation for the company's refusal to drop its bans on autonomous lethal weapons and mass surveillance, though a parallel case keeps the designation technically alive.

pull_quote.text: The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics.

data_points.label: Red lines Anthropic refused to drop

stories.article_excerpt: The order landed on a Thursday night, 59 pages long, and it did something no court had yet done.

stories.headline: White House Weighs Extending Chip Tariffs to Finished Servers and Laptops, Threatening AI Buildout Costs
stories.key_takeaway: A second round of Section 232 semiconductor tariffs under discussion would extend duties to finished AI servers, laptops and consoles, and could eliminate the data-center exemption that has shielded US AI infrastructure spending since January.

pull_quote.text: Anytime you add to the cost and decrease predictability, you make it more difficult to invest, and you are putting that in jeopardy.

stories.article_excerpt: Seven months after imposing a deliberately narrow 25% tariff on a thin slice of advanced AI chips, officials are weighing a wider net.

stories.headline: More Than 100 Companies Sign a Joint Call to Defend Critical Infrastructure From AI-Powered Attacks
stories.key_takeaway: An open letter signed by more than 100 companies warns that AI-enabled attacks on hospitals, water systems and internet infrastructure will surge within months, but attaches no commitments, deadlines or funding to the appeal.

pull_quote.text: I can tell you without exaggeration that we believe that this is a generational shift in cybersecurity.

stories.article_excerpt: More than 100 of the world's largest technology and cybersecurity companies signed a joint open letter on Thursday.

stories.headline: UK Actors Demand Legal Ownership of Their Voices as AI Cloning Scams Spread
stories.key_takeaway: Around 80 UK performers are asking the government to create a statutory personality right over a person's voice, arguing existing copyright and data protection law leaves synthetic replicas effectively unregulated.

pull_quote.text: My voice is unique. It is mine. It is part of my identity. So is yours. That is worth speaking up about.

data_points.label: UK adults targeted by voice scams

stories.article_excerpt: Around 80 British actors, narrators, singers and comedians have signed an open letter to the Prime Minister.
